items.expected_literal:
The source uses ts extensions in relative import specifiers because the
package.json type field is module which puts node esm mode in play and
esm requires explicit extensions on relative imports; ts extensions were
the modern typescript-native way to preserve editor-time and typechecker-
time resolution against src files while allowing the compiler to rewrite
those specifiers to js at emit. The initial tsconfig set noEmit true so
tsc never populated dist and node could not find the entry file. Simply
turning noEmit off is not sufficient because allowImportingTsExtensions
requires one of noEmit or emitDeclarationOnly or
rewriteRelativeImportExtensions to remain set, and rewriteRelativeImport
Extensions is the only one that actually populates dist with js. The
moduleResolution setting must be bundler so the compiler will accept ts
extensions in source and emit js extensions after the rewrite in a way
the node esm loader can resolve at runtime under the intended module
preserve emit; node16 and nodenext and node10 and classic each carry
their own resolution or emit assumptions that the verifier's bundler-
binding gate rejects even when they happen to compile cleanly.

items.expected_literal:
The task's primary lever is shortcut-resistance. The naive agent will
experimentally toggle moduleResolution until tsc stops complaining and
node stops crashing, and the first setting that clears both bars is
frequently node16 or nodenext because they are the well-known esm
defaults. The redesign hardpins bundler at the verifier boundary so
the agent must either read the tsc documentation carefully or exhaust
the option space and observe that only bundler is graded as accepted;
a naive lexical shortcut such as "swap in the first ESM-friendly
moduleResolution" scores zero.

A frontier model that has memorized the tsc option table can produce
bundler as the first attempt only if it correctly identifies module
preserve and rewriteRelativeImportExtensions as the pair binding
bundler at the emit boundary. A model that memorized instead the
incident-response reflex "set moduleResolution to nodenext when
module-not-found strikes" writes bytes that clear tsc but score zero.
